decisions.reason: This product extends the firm's core substrate and wafer-packaging capabilities and fits customers' demand for higher-functionality wafer-level solutions, so a specialized supplier would usually retain it unless volumes disappoint badly.

Carrier wafers for handling smaller-diameter wafers are very close to the firm's established business and to its stated direction in reusable carriers and thin-wafer handling, making withdrawal unlikely.

The Cu-interposer glass wafer is technically ambitious and may still be ramping commercially, but it is well aligned with the firm's R&D profile and strategic move toward multifunctional packaging wafers.
An off-the-shelf brand for standard glass and quartz wafers broadens commercialization of the firm's existing know-how with limited strategic risk, so management would likely continue it.

Glass-based circuit boards are materially related but commercially more distant from the firm's narrow core wafer-substrate business, so a focused German specialist would be relatively likely to exit and reallocate resources.
